model.name: Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base
model.dtype_note: the checkpoint ships in bfloat16, so bfloat16 is its full precision; float32 would need ~7.7 GB of weights and does not fit the 8 GB RTX 2080 SUPER
model.speaker_similarity: cosine of Qwen3-TTS speaker embeddings (first 8 s) vs the owner reference
model.loudness: ffmpeg ebur128 (ITU-R BS.1770 integrated LUFS, 4x-oversampled true peak)

owner.use: warm rows; speaker-similarity target for every row
owner.transcript: FrankenWhisper (fw transcribe, whisper.cpp backend, ggml-large-v3) on the Mac; the stored transcript matches it, and faster-whisper large-v3 on eris agrees at the WER shown (the text and audio stay private)

excited.pipeline: Qwen3-TTS VoiceDesign (high-energy announcer instruction) -> Seed-VC F0-conditioned conversion into the owner's timbre, +4 semitones (voice_energy.py --vc-mode f0 --lift 4)
excited.text: And they're off! What a start from number seven, flat out into the first corner! Oh, he's sideways, he's sideways, and he holds it! Unbelievable! Here comes the pack, doors flying everywhere, this is absolutely bonkers! What a race!

selection.rule: zero WER on every experiment take, at least +2 semitones median pitch over the owner (it must sound excited), then best mean speaker similarity

export.process: trim silence (-42 dB rel. peak; 60 ms lead, 160 ms tail, 30 ms fade-out) -> gain to target + sample-peak limiter -> libopus -> decode and re-measure, iterate

screens.pick_rule: Among takes passing the wer, speaker_sim, duration and raw_loudness screens, the highest score = 0.6*(1-min(wer,1)) + 0.4*speaker_sim (+ 0.1*clip(lift_st/8,0,1) for hype rows); ties to the lower seed. If no take passes, the row fails and the best score overall is kept for the record. The export screen (decoded Opus LUFS and true peak) is checked on the picked take.
